items.description: An employee was terminated shortly after raising a protected complaint. The case settled after the employer's stated reason failed to match the documented timeline.
A jury found that an employee's demotion and eventual termination followed directly after reporting safety violations to a supervisor.
A group of warehouse employees recovered unpaid overtime after being required to work off the clock during shift changes.
A healthcare worker was denied a reasonable accommodation and later terminated. The verdict addressed the employer's failure to engage in the interactive process.
An employee reported a hostile work environment created by a supervisor. The employer had not investigated the earlier complaint.
A group of construction workers treated as independent contractors recovered unpaid overtime, expense reimbursement, and penalties after being reclassified as employees.
An employee was passed over for promotion multiple times despite strong reviews, with the pattern tracking closely to a protected characteristic.
An employee returning from CFRA baby-bonding leave was not reinstated to a comparable position, contrary to what the law requires.
A departing executive's severance offer was renegotiated after review revealed the release language was broader than legally required.

items.classification: PAGA Wage and Hour Group Claim
items.description: A representative action recovered civil penalties for a group of employees after a company-wide meal break policy failed to comply with California law.
